claims.statement: Algolia documents a Monitoring API key that authenticates requests to the Monitoring API infrastructure endpoints, sent in the x-algolia-api-key header.

sources.supports: To authenticate requests to the Infrastructure endpoints, add these headers: x-algolia-application-id (your Algolia application ID) and x-algolia-api-key (your Monitoring API key).
Other API keys: Monitoring API key.

claims.statement: Algolia states the metrics exposed by the Monitoring API come from external monitoring probes checking Algolia's infrastructure, reflect overall infrastructure status and do not represent the performance of the specific application ID used for authentication, and that endpoints other than the Infrastructure endpoints require no authentication.

sources.supports: The metrics exposed by this API are based on results from external monitoring probes checking Algolia’s infrastructure. These metrics reflect the overall infrastructure status and don’t represent the performance of the specific APPID used for authentication.

claims.statement: Algolia states access to the Monitoring API Infrastructure endpoints is available as part of the Premium or Elevate plans, and gives https://status.algolia.com as its base URL.

sources.supports: Access to the Infrastructure endpoints is available as part of the Premium or Elevate plans.

claims.statement: Algolia recommends regenerating all API keys at least once a year and limiting each key's validity to one year, and its API reference states that by default a key does not expire.

sources.supports: Regenerate all your API keys at least once a year. Rotating your API keys reduces the risk of leaks, misuse, and compliance issues. For sensitive apps, rotate your keys more often. Limit each API key’s validity to one year.
Duration (in seconds) after which the API key expires. By default, API keys don't expire.

openQuestions.question: This candidate is established only as existing: the prefix, alphabet, length and structure of the value are not documented on the pages read and are not researched.

The pages read do not say whether Algolia keys of different roles share one value shape; role must not be attributed from shape alone, and identification needs the surrounding context (header, variable name, ACL).

The ACL list on the pages read has no monitoring entry, so which ACL, if any, the Monitoring API key carries, and whether it is created through the same key-creation endpoint as other keys, is not stated.

Whether Algolia expects the Monitoring API key to be kept confidential is not stated on the pages read. The low scope the page describes (infrastructure status, not customer data) is a documented property of the API, not a handling instruction.
